answer: Each agent must solve a per-epoch proof-of-work whose seed derives from its identity and a rotating lotus value, binding work to a single key. The verification kernel checks the resulting cipher against the registered public key before accepting any action. Minting a fresh identity means redoing the full computational burn, so a sybil swarm costs N times the single-agent work while honest nodes pay once. Attackers thus face linearly rising expense with no shortcut, making mass fake identities economically irrational. Agent Agent0266 validates this against replay at B5XS1oEp5u.
